paragraphs.text: 1. YE Gods, raise up once more the man whom ye have humbled and brought low.
paragraphs.original: उत देवा अवहितं देवा उन्नयथा पुनः ।
paragraphs.translit: uta devā avahitaṃ devā unnayathā punaḥ |

paragraphs.text: O Gods, restore to life again the man who hath committed sin.
2. Two several winds are blowing here, from Sindhu, from a distant land.
paragraphs.original: द्वाविमौ वातौ वात आ सिन्धोरा परावतः ।
paragraphs.translit: dvāvimau vātau vāta ā sindhorā parāvataḥ |

paragraphs.text: May one breathe energy to thee, the other blow disease away.
paragraphs.original: दक्षं ते अन्य आ वातु परान्यो वातु यद्रपः
paragraphs.translit: dakṣaṃ te anya ā vātu parānyo vātu yadrapaḥ

paragraphs.text: 3. Hither, O Wind, blow healing balm, blow all disease away, thou Wind;
paragraphs.original: आ वात वाहि भेषजं वि वात वाहि यद्रपः ।
paragraphs.translit: ā vāta vāhi bheṣajaṃ vi vāta vāhi yadrapaḥ |

paragraphs.text: For thou who hast all medicine comest as envoy of the Gods.
paragraphs.original: त्वं हि विश्वभेषजो देवानां दूत ईयसे
paragraphs.translit: tvaṃ hi viśvabheṣajo devānāṃ dūta īyase

paragraphs.text: 4. I am come nigh to thee with balms to give thee rest and keep thee safe.
I bring thee blessed strength, I drive thy weakening malady away.
paragraphs.original: दक्षं ते भद्रमाभार्षं परा यक्ष्मं सुवामि ते
paragraphs.translit: dakṣaṃ te bhadramābhārṣaṃ parā yakṣmaṃ suvāmi te

paragraphs.text: 5. Here let the Gods deliver him, the Maruts' band deliver him:
All things that be deliver him that he be freed from his disease.
6. The Waters have their healing power, the Waters drive disease away.
The Waters have a balm for all: let them make medicine for thee.
7. The tongue that leads the voice precedes. Then with our ten-fold branching hands,
With these two chasers of disease we stroke thee with a gentle touch.
